description: Hand-curated core of the FR golden set: the parameter families the JRC asked for by name (barème IR, CDHR, CEHR, minimum wage, PSS), each pinned to its OpenFisca-France counterpart. build-openfisca-dataset drafts a case per entry and tops the set up from params.parameter_links. Every drafted case is verified:false until a human confirms it in the UI's Golden set tab.

conventions.temporal_basis: Taken from the parameter record, never from this file: income_year parameters expect the OpenFisca value keyed <year>-01-01 (income year), in_force ones the value in force at as_of.
conventions.factor: euromod_value = factor * openfisca_value. EUROMOD stores several SIC ceilings as multiples of the monthly PSS.
conventions.component: 'value' for scalars, 'brackets[i].<field>' for one band of an OpenFisca scale, 'brackets' for the whole schedule.
conventions.source: Every entry resolves through the parameter store: `model_target` for a single parameter in params.parameters, `group_id` for a bracket schedule assembled from params.parameter_groups (with `model_target` pinning the assembled record's established identity). No entry reads a hand-authored parameter file.

entries.note: Barème IR as one table case, assembled from params.parameter_groups FR:tinkt_fr:tin_schedule (bands 1/3/4/5/6 of the export's own schedule definition). EUROMOD's 2025 thresholds are one euro below CGI art. 197 — a known error on the EUROMOD side, to be corrected by the economists team, so the expected value is the law's.

Barème IR band 1 upper limit. EUROMOD holds the schedule applied in the system year (previous year's income); the income-year convention expects the following finance act's value. EUROMOD's 2025 value is one euro below the law (a known EUROMOD-side error, being corrected by the economists team); the expected value is the law's.
Barème IR band 3 upper limit. EUROMOD's 2025 value is one euro below the law (a known EUROMOD-side error, being corrected by the economists team); the expected value is the law's.
Barème IR band 4 upper limit. EUROMOD's 2025 value is one euro below the law (a known EUROMOD-side error, being corrected by the economists team); the expected value is the law's.
Barème IR band 5 upper limit. EUROMOD's 2025 value is one euro below the law (a known EUROMOD-side error, being corrected by the economists team); the expected value is the law's.
Barème IR rate of the exempt band (0). A rate that must NOT move — the revalorisation touches thresholds only.
Barème IR rate of band 2 (11%). EUROMOD's band 2 slot ($tin_rate2) was abolished in 2015, so band numbering differs by one from OpenFisca's.
Barème IR rate of band 3 (30%).
Barème IR rate of band 4 (41%).
Barème IR top rate (45%).
Décote ceiling, single taxpayer.
Décote ceiling, couple.
Quotient familial ceiling, single parent.
Quotient familial ceiling, general half-share.

CDHR: instituted by LF 2025 (14 Feb 2025) FOR 2025 income — the case that exercises the income-year budget-act window and the year-naming extract exemption. Defined inside tinto01_fr, so it reaches params.parameters via extracted_parameters/curated/FR.in_function.json.
CEHR first threshold, single (250 000 €). Unchanged since 2011 — a no-change case on an income-year parameter.
CEHR second threshold single / first threshold couple (500 000 €).
CEHR second threshold, couple (1 000 000 €).
CEHR first rate (3%).
CEHR second rate (4%).
SMIC, gross monthly. Revalorised by décret, not by an annual act, and 2025 saw no January raise — the value in force comes from the November 2024 décret.
SMIC, gross hourly — the value the décret actually states; the monthly figure is derived from it.
Plafond annuel de la sécurité sociale, fixed each December by arrêté.
SIC income limit: 1x the monthly PSS.
SIC income limit: 3x the monthly PSS. The arrêté states the ceiling once; the multiple is EUROMOD's — a derived-value case.
Complementary-pension income limit: 1x the monthly PSS.
Complementary-pension income limit: 4x the monthly PSS.
Complementary-pension income limit: 8x the monthly PSS.
